explanation: The Y181V mutation removes the bulky aromatic tyrosine ring and its hydroxyl group, creating a smaller hydrophobic pocket that weakens van der Waals contacts with efavirenz at the NNRTI binding site—the 53.6 Å³ volume reduction and direct ligand contact (3.8 Å minimum distance) indicate that efavirenz loses favorable interactions with the aromatic π-system and potential hydrogen bonding with the tyrosine hydroxyl. Although the energetic penalty is modest (-0.03 kcal/mol), this reflects a subtle loss of binding complementarity rather than a dramatic clash, as the smaller valine accommodates the ligand without introducing steric strain—the resistance mechanism operates through cumulative reduction in favorable interactions rather than allosteric destabilization.
